title: Streaming callback + resumable resume protocol (scratch)
body:
Goal:
Lightweight protocol for server-initiated streaming callbacks (webhook style) that supports client-side resumability of partially received responses. Use case: mobile/embedded SDKs that prefer server push but need to reconnect and resume mid-response without re-generating from scratch.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-client sync (we don't attempt CRDTs)
- Replacing existing SSE/WebSocket SDKs for always-on clients

Constraints and assumptions:
- Clients may lose network for N minutes (configurable).
- Server keeps short-lived resume state (KV) for up to resume_ttl (default 15 minutes).
- Resume is best-effort: if state is gone, fallback to deterministic retry or idempotent request semantics.
- Auth must be simple (JWT with intent scope) to avoid handshake complexity on mobile.

High-level ideas:
1) Each streaming request gets a server-generated resume_token returned to the client on first callback.
2) Callbacks carry an incremental chunk index and an optional checkpoint hash.
3) Client acknowledges final receipt (ACK) so server can free state early.
4) If the client reconnects it can call the Resume endpoint with resume_token and last_chunk_id it received; server replays from next chunk or resumes generation if supported by runtime KV-cache.

API shapes (sketch):
- POST /v1/infer (normal request) returns: 200 + streaming callback target & resume_token if client requested push
  response example: {
    "request_id": "r_123",
    "callback_target": "https://client.example/webhook",
    "resume_token": "rt_abc",
    "resume_ttl_seconds": 900
  }

- Callback envelope (server -> client webhook):
  POST to callback_target with JSON body:
  {
    "resume_token": "rt_abc",
    "chunk_id": 0,
    "chunk_type": "delta",        // delta | final | checkpoint
    "payload": "text chunk...",
    "checkpoint_hash": "sha256:..."  // optional, can be used for verification
  }

- Client resumes (client -> Redwood):
  POST /v1/infer/resume
  body: { "resume_token": "rt_abc", "last_seen_chunk_id": 2 }
  server response: either 200 + list of missing chunks OR 202 + new resume_token if server will continue generation async.

State model on server:
- resume_key -> { request_id, last_chunk_id_sent, checkpoint_hash, callback_target, created_at }
- Chunks are transient (not stored long-term) but optionally buffered to a short-term chunk store (TTL ~ 15m) for replay when resume requested. If chunk store disabled, server can only resume if runtime supports generation continuation via KV cache (backend-dependent).

Client lifecycle diagram (ascii):
Client            Server                ChunkStore/KV
  |                 |                        |
  | POST /infer    |                        |
  |--------------->| create resume_token    |
  |                 | send streaming cbks -->| store chunks (optional)
  |                 |                        |
  | receives chunk0 |                        |
  | lose connectivity (t1)                   |
  | reconnect (t2)  |                        |
  | POST /infer/resume -------------------->| lookup resume_key
  |                 | 200 + missing chunks   |  return chunk1..n
  |                 |                        |

Edge cases and decisions to make:
- When to buffer chunks? (default: buffer only up to 2MB or X chunks; configurable per-customer).
- Checkpoint hash mismatch: treat as a divergence signal — either request full restart or try to fast-forward. Need policy.
- Duplicate delivery: clients must de-duplicate by resume_token + chunk_id.
- Multiple client endpoints: allow registering multiple callback_targets for the same resume_token? Probably no — encourages one receiver per resume_token to keep semantics simple.
- Backpressure: if client ACK lags, server should slow down generation (apply backpressure via runtime) or buffer to chunk store until limit.

Security model:
- Resume token encoded as signed JWT: "rt_<base64>" containing request_id, expiry, intent scope, signature_ver. Server validates on resume.
- Callback authenticity: Redwood signs payloads with ephemeral HMAC key and includes header X-RWD-Signature so clients can verify origin (useful for mobile).
- Rate-limiting resume attempts per token to avoid brute-force.

Metrics to collect:
- resume_requested_count, resume_success_count, resume_failure_count (reason tags: ttl_expired, missing_chunks, auth_fail)
- avg_resume_replay_size, avg_time_between_disconnect_and_resume
- chunk_store_hit_rate (how often replay served from buffer vs runtime continuation)

Implementation experiments (quick plan):
- Phase A (quick proto): server buffers chunks to Redis list with TTL; resume reads missing items. No runtime continuation yet. Use signed opaque resume_token.
- Phase B: hook into runtime KV continuation so resume can continue generation from cache if buffer missing. Need runtime API: continue_from(request_id, last_token_index).
- Phase C: allow clients to request partial deterministic re-generation (if models are deterministic w/ same seed) as fallback when buffer/continuation unavailable.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Spike: small PoC using Redis list as chunk buffer (Mateo) — estimate 2 days.
- [ ] Draft JWT resume_token format + crypto header (Evelyn).
- [ ] Add instrumentation hooks in console to show resume events (product/ops ask).
- [ ] Define TTL policy per-customer with defaults and cost model.

Notes / open questions:
- Is resume_token a public-facing API concept or internal? If public, storage and rotation policies more complicated (rotation of signing key).
- How to handle large attachments (images/audio) in chunk store? Maybe require client to fetch via presigned url instead of embedding binary in callback requests.
- Should we expose a WebSocket fallback for always-on clients that want lower-latency resume? Probably separate path.

References / related tickets / prototypes in drive: see linked_artifacts.

Quick developer cheat-sheet for client SDK implementers:
- on initial infer -> register webhook + pass "push_mode": true in request body.
- expect envelope chunks; store last_chunk_id persisted to disk (atomic write).
- on network reconnect -> call /infer/resume with last_chunk_id. If server returns replay chunk list, apply them in order and continue normal handling. If server returns 202 (server will continue), wait for new callbacks.
- always verify X-RWD-Signature header on callback.

This doc is a rough scratchpad. Goal is to validate the UX with a quick PoC before spec'ing in more detail. Keep it lightweight and iterate after prototype results.

Random implementation notes from convo with runtime team:
- runtime can emit stable chunk ids if we adopt an internal token counter per request. That plus a KV-cache key per request_id might be enough to support resume without chunk buffering (CF: DEV-3004).
- chunk buffering adds cost but simplifies client experience; allow it as an opt-in per customer.

End of scratchpad.
